prerequisites: Good knowledge in college math and physics

Good knowledge in applied math (differential and integral calculus in 1,2,3 variables, vector algebra and analysis, complex number and complex exponentials, simple differential equations, Fourier transform)
Good knowledge and ability on circuit theory, especially AC circuits

learning_outcomes.text: Students must know the properties of electromagnetic fields and the main devices that use them.
Students must be able to correctly evaluate the effects of electromagnetic phenomena on the behavior of ICT (and, more generally, electronic) equipments.
At the end of the course the student will have developed the ability to find and apply standard solutions to the different cases that he may face, and to evaluate their feasibility.
The knowledge acquired will allow the student to subsequently deal with the study and integration of equipment, systems and services that use electromagnetic fields.

The acquired knowledge will be useful to those who will not deal directly with these activities, as it will allow future engineers to interact efficiently with the designers of electromagnetic devices, which are increasingly widespread in all electronic and ICT systems, as well as in many systems of diagnostics and measurement, particularly in the physical and biomedical fields.

assessment_rules: The exam is a written test. To pass the exam, a minimum of 5 points in the multiple-choice questions part and at least 8 points in the numerical exercise part are required, with a final score of 18 or more. The final score is the sum of the results of the two parts, plus 0.15 points, rounded to the closest integer. To obtain "30 cum laude" it will be necessary to reach a final score of at least 32 points.
